_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Zelda II - The Adventure of Link (ADR-0239,
PRD F14.16's wave three). Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
This file is data. A second game is a second file beside this one - no code
change - as long as its navigation address and every value it is set to are
read off a published RAM map or the vendored cheat database (ADR-0184 s5:
no code is invented). It is a SECOND profile in this folder, not a
replacement for the stage set: field.txt, field-probe.txt and mint-field.txt
keep the routes and the declared ROM hash they already had, and nothing here
adds a rooms[] key, so scripts/library_job.start_plan resolves every route
exactly as it did before.
Rung (ADR-0239 s1's ladder). Rung 2: a published RAM selector, pinned for
the run. Rung 1 was checked first and is not available for this ROM. The
game's own selector is the file menu, and it selects one of three save
files, not a place: every file starts in North Castle's throne room, which
is what the stage set's own mint-field.txt already plays. There is no level
select, no password and no continue code in the US ROM (the Famicom disk
version's save files are the closest thing, and they are save data, not a
selector). Rung 3 (a save state reached by search, chain or movie) is the
tool for a room no selector reaches, out of this slice's scope, and is not
used here.
Selector and values. $0748 is the area the game loads into its sideview.
Almar's Guides' Action Replay page 'Sidescrolling Stage Level Modifier'
enumerates it value by value from 0748:00 through 0748:7E - 65 rows plus the
page's own header - and names every place in English; DataCrystal's RAM map
corroborates the address from the other side: '$0748 - area location index
(the index of the spot on the overworld that pulled you into the sideview)',
and its '$056C - Palace Code' is the byte the palace values land on. Both
pages are cited in full in navigation.source below; the rows this profile
uses are quoted verbatim in each value's title. Two published sources
agree, and nothing here is invented (ADR-0184 s5).
WHAT IS SWEPT, AND WHAT IS LEFT OUT. Every value whose place is a room the
game draws and a player can stand in: the three palace interiors, Kings
Tomb, the four towns, the nine dark caverns, the two bat caverns, the four
bridged rocky areas, the long bridge, the raft port, the rocky areas, the
graveyard, the swamp, the desert, the Stonehenge field, the fairy field, the
tree-stump field and the mountain path - 36 values.
Left out, with the reason, so a later slice does not have to re-derive it:
00, 2E  'Princess Zelda Sleeping' - the vanilla start. The throne room is
where field.txt's own run begins, so these two are the BEFORE
side of the measurement (ADR-0239 s5) and not a place this sweep
warps to. s4 would score them as adding nothing the baseline does
not already hold.
01, 03  'Dark Cavern Stage ?' - the two values Almar's page could not
name, both ending in a question mark. 0A-12 already cover the
nine caverns the page does name.
02, 04, the enemy-variant duplicates of a room a listed value already
1A, 19, sweeps: 02 'Grassy Forest Area At Night, With Cyan Bats' and 04
20, 31, '... Blue Jumping Enemies' are 06's field; 1A 'In Grassy Field At
70      Night, With Tree Stumps, With Blue Jumping Enemies' is 06's; 19
'Fairie Out In Grassy Field At Night (No Tree Stumps)' is 17's;
20 'Sand Dunes, Beside Link Doll' is 1E's; 31 'In Water Town of
Saria (Different)' is 30's; 70 'Rocky Area With Bridge, Red Dog
(?) Enemy Nearby' is 15's. s5's union counts a room once, and the
enemies are sprites the run draws wherever it is.
27      'Falling Cutscene, Dark Caverns (Near A Red Potion Container)' -
the cavern it lands in is one of the nine.
1F, 21, 'Stuck In Mountains' / 'Stuck In Ocean' / 'Stuck In A Mountain
22, 41, (Near A Town)' / 'Stuck In A Rock On An Island' / 'Stuck In A
37, 55, Swamp On Map' - places the game drops Link inside a collision
5E, 6E  tile with no way out. 37's own title ('3D: In The Middle of
Nowhere, Stuck In Mountains') is the same place as 1F, 21 and 22.
They draw one screen of terrain nobody can play, and a warp to
one is indistinguishable from a broken run.
3F, 40, 'Falling Cutscene' variants. 4E and 56 are pure cutscenes with no
4E, 4F, playable room at all; 3F and 4F land in the throne room, and 40
56      in the ocean, all three already named above or below.
7E      'Crashes (Dark Screen)' - a dark screen, which is a crash and not
a place.
(rest)  the 59 values in 0x38-0x7D the page does not enumerate at all
0x71-0x7D): the page names 65 of the byte's 256 values and 11 of
those lie in this range, which holds 70. No published source
names the rest, so no value is set to one (ADR-0184 s5).
09 is listed even though its title ('Lone Grave On Red Bricks, With Purple
Background And Green Ground') reads like a room from a cutscene: it is a
distinct tileset on the overworld, and if the session turns out to draw no
new art, s4's `new` count reports that as a figure beside the tiles rather
than as a silent omission. 05, 26 and 3E are listed for the same reason.
The stage-clear transition is never recorded by any session of this sweep:
the selector is pinned for the whole run, so the game never observes the
place advancing (ADR-0184's 2026-09-14 amendment). Deaths and respawns are
still recorded - the blind body dies on most places - so ADR-0184 s4 is met,
and the stage set's own field.txt route still records the death screen as it
always did.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply and is not run.
A published lives address does exist - the vendored database
(UI/Dependencies/Internal/CheatDb.Nes.json) ships 'Infinite lives (alt)' as
0700:04 - but s3 admits a lives pin only behind a four-arm, byte-identical
textures/ comparison, and a pin that fails it is not a pin this sweep may
carry. Without one the blind body is allowed to die and to reach GAME OVER,
which is what ADR-0184 s4 asks for. The database's own entry is keyed to a
different dump (sha1 52BF22C47D86DBD1E09A9179EDD593B19E43115B) than this
one, which is a second reason not to reach into it for a pin.

_provenanceComment: romSha1 is the No-Intro SHA1 the stage set already pins
(scripts/stages/zelda2/stage-set.json), and the library dump it names is the
one this sweep recorded - checked before anything ran, so a sweep of a
different dump could not be reported under this hash. The whole-file SHA1 of
the same library file is 353489A57F24A429572E76BD455BC51D821F7036, which is
also the <supportedRom> every bootstrapped pack of this sweep carries: the
builder stamps the loaded file's own SHA1 over the pack's declaration, which
is the same two-hash split ADR-0003 draws and the cause of issue #314. The
ROM is the user's own dump and is never copied into the repository.

_ramCheckComment: Each value's ramCheck reads one byte off the session's OWN final state
(<session>/rec-final.mss, written by the sweep's save-state= because the
run reached its frame target). Neither byte is the selector's address, so
neither carries ADR-0239 s4's pinnedValue caveat: $0748 is pinned and
substituted on the CPU read bus, and a check on it could not tell the
game's own value from a byte the game stored after reading the pin.
Eight values read $056C - the three palaces plus Kings Tomb and the four
towns - because the expectation is a formula DataCrystal publishes rather
than a guess: its $056C gloss is 'Palace index on continent
($748 - #$34)'. MEASURED at this profile's own shape (mint-field.txt +
field.txt repeated, 120 s), the identity holds on the game's own final
-> FF. Eight for eight, read off eight final states with one command. Note
what the identity is and is not: the value is the game's own record of the
area the pin selected, taken modulo a byte, so for a place whose index is
below $34 it is a large number and names no palace - it is the arithmetic
that is published, and that is what these checks assert. It also survives
the body walking Link one screen east or west, which moves $0748 and
leaves $056C at what the loaded area put there (rauru, ruto and mido all
end one screen on). $0748 itself ends at the pinned byte in most of the 36
and at a neighbouring screen's index in the rest, so it is not a check this
profile can assert one value for; the fingerprints in
runs/f1418/zelda2/RESULT.md tabulate it.
The first recorded pass of this profile read $0707 for all five of those
non-palace values and five checks came back FAIL: the four town sessions
ended with $0707 = 0 and Kings Tomb with $0707 = 1, against the published
gloss of the byte ('0=caves, enemy encounters; 1=west hyrule towns;
2=east hyrule towns'). The gloss did not hold for an interior, so those
five moved to the instrument the states can prove. The readings are kept in
RESULT.md rather than deleted: they are the measurement that retired the
expectation.
The remaining 27 values read $0707, DataCrystal's '"world"', expecting 0 -
its published meaning for 'caves, enemy encounters', which is what a cave,
a rocky area, a bridge, a field, the swamp and the desert are. It is one
byte shared by the places of one world, so it is a weaker check than
$056C and it is deliberately not narrowed to a guess: what it proves is
that the session ended on the kind of ground the value named, and a session
that crashed reads outside the set. That the vanilla throne room also reads
$0707 = 0 - the baseline's own reading - is the honest limit of this check
on a cave or field value: it does not, on its own, separate a warped cave
from a did-not-warp. ADR-0239 s4's `new` count is the gate that does (every
one of the 36 passes it), and the no-pin control at
runs/f1418/zelda2/probe/nopin is what says the vanilla state is the one
this byte cannot separate. This check is reported beside the gate, exactly
as Excitebike's profile reports its two shared mode bytes.
Per-value fingerprints - the $0748, $0561 and $056B each 120 s session
actually ended on - are read off the same final states and tabulated in
runs/f1418/zelda2/RESULT.md. They are the evidence that no two values of
this sweep ended in the same place by accident, and they are not checks
here because a check is one address and the table needs three.
A failing check is not always a broken run: a body that walks Link off the
right edge moves him to the next sideview screen, and the game then writes
the next area's $0748. Where a session did that, the check reports it and
the final state's own $0748 says how far it got.
_defaultsComment: The entry is the stage set's own mint script, unchanged, and it runs as
INPUT rather than as a state: a navigation session starts from power-on with
the pin already set, and the boot's own load is what the pin steers (ADR-0239
s2 puts entry and body in the profile for exactly this). No save state is
used, so nothing unversioned has to travel with this profile.
mint-field.txt is 904 frames - power-on through the title, the register
screen, a named file and three Starts into the throne room - and both of its
halves are load-bearing: a file the game has not named cannot be selected, so
a shorter entry never leaves the menu (scripts/stages/README.md, 'Zelda II:
the menu is the hard part'). field.txt is the set's gameplay route, 4420
frames, repeated by record_navigation_sweep.py until the 120 s budget is
covered; it leaves the castle, walks east and then alternates wandering the
grass with a short fight, which is what the recorder needs (a figure's cycle
needs two turns of a hold).
It is a blind body on every place but its own: it holds Right and hops, which
is not what clears a palace or a cavern, so most sessions end in a death
rather than at the next screen. That is the same trade Contra's and Ninja
Gaiden's profiles make, and it is why s4's `new` count, not the body, is what
